Alleviate

/uh-LEE-vee-ayt/ - the stress falls on LEE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Alleviate means to make pain, worry, or hardship easier to bear.

The city's new express lane did nothing to fix the narrow bridge itself, but it alleviated the worst of the rush-hour crawl.

Worked Example

Nothing on the pharmacy shelf could shrink the cast on Dara's arm or hurry the bone's knitting; the wedge her brother rigged from couch cushions simply alleviated the throbbing enough for her to sit through class and take notes left-handed.

Alleviate is the precise choice because it means to lighten a burden without removing it — the break still has to mend on its own. Cure would overclaim, and comfort is vaguer; alleviate names real, partial relief.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

ease: the everyday word for the same lightening, softer in tone

relieve: often stronger — relief can be total, while alleviating is usually partial

lighten: borrowed from physical weight; you lighten a load, alleviate a pain

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

worsen: to push the pain or problem the other way

deepen: to make the suffering sink in further

Where it sits · how much of the burden is lifted — soothe → alleviate → cure

soothe vs. alleviate: Soothing is gentler than alleviating — a kind word or a cool cloth calms the feeling for a moment without making the burden itself any lighter.

cure vs. alleviate: Cure goes further than alleviate — alleviating lightens what you carry while the cause remains, but a cure takes the cause away altogether.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — al-

Prefix — al-: to, toward (a form of ad-)

Root — levi-

Root — levi-: light in weight (Latin levis)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb: to make, to cause

Put it together

Put it together: Al- (toward) + levi- (light) + -ate (to make) = to make light. Latin levis, 'light in weight,' is the same root that lets a magician levitate and a joke bring levity to a meeting. To alleviate a burden is literally to take weight off it — not to take it away.

Use the root in a new word: levity

Use the root in a new word: levity: A little levity from the coach — one bad pun — loosened up the whole locker room before the final.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

This unit carries four cousins, so keep their lanes straight. Alleviate lightens a burden for the one who bears it; mitigate softens the force of the harmful thing itself; palliate eases symptoms while openly leaving the cause untreated; ameliorate lifts a whole bad situation. Reach for alleviate when someone's pain, fear, or load gets lighter but the source remains.
